title: fix(plugin-security): carry renamed position holders after a hot install, not only at boot
body:
Part of #33238

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：岗位声明 `renamedFrom` 后，平台把旧名任职人迁到新名。这一步原来只在内核启动时跑；现在运行中的内核收到 `metadata:reloaded` 宣告后也会跑，但只判定宣告点名、且此刻仍在注册中的那个包或那个岗位所声明的改名。
- 为什么改：热安装进运行中环境的应用，旧名任职人原本要等下次重启才迁；本次让市场本地安装与逐项发布立刻生效。热升级（旧版本仍在服务）、运行时 `POST /packages` 安装与启用这几条路径仍是重启时迁，所以本卡保持打开。
- 风险与回滚：这是一次以系统身份改变「谁持有岗位」的写入。reload 只判定宣告点名的范围，判定规则与启动时完全相同（停用不复活、不认领别人的旧名等）；卸载类宣告不迁任何人。回滚即回退本 PR，行为回到只在启动时迁。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/position-renamed-holder-carry.ts` 中的 `positionRenameReloadScope` 与 `carryRenamedPositionHolders` 的 `only` 过滤；`security-plugin-start-hooks.ts` 的 `metadata:reloaded` 钩子；测试文件末尾「condition 2 on the reload path」一例。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/position-renamed-holder-carry.test.ts`，预期 35 个用例全绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

`plugin-security`'s `renamedFrom` holder carry (ruling A1 on #32983) ran only at `kernel:bootstrapped`. It now also runs on `metadata:reloaded` after the boot run. A reload run judges only the renames declared by what the announcement names as registered at that moment. Ruling condition 2, that a package never claims an old name it did not own, therefore holds on the reload path exactly as on the boot path.

- `positionRenameReloadScope(payload, engine)` reads the scope from the payload's `changed` list:
  - `app/ID` counts only while the registry holds package `ID` (`registry.getPackage`).
  - `position/NAME` counts when NAME is in position-name grammar.
  - Every other entry names nothing.
- `carryRenamedPositionHolders(engine, deps, { only })` drops every old name that no in-scope position claims. The refusals are still judged against the whole catalog, the disabled packages' positions and the activation ledger.
- `createPositionRenameCarryRuns`:
  - `afterReload(payload)` reads the scope when the announcement arrives. An empty scope reads nothing and carries nothing.
  - A reload run reads the references it would leave behind only for old names it moved rows of (`leftBehindOnlyWhenMoved`).
  - The boot run is unchanged: it is unscoped and names left-behind references as ruled.
  - Runs stay serialized and stay ignored before the boot run. A warning the previous run gave is not repeated.

What each announcer on `origin/main` puts in the payload, and what a reload run does with it:

| Announcer | Payload `changed` | Reload run |
|---|---|---|
| marketplace install-local, hot install or upgrade (`announceHotInstall`) | `app/MANIFESTID`, after register | judges that package's positions |
| marketplace install-local, uninstall | `app/MANIFESTID`, after the registry withdrawal | the package is no longer held: carries nothing |
| per-item publish (`ObjectQLPlugin.announcePerItemPublish`) | `TYPE/NAME` | `position/NAME`: judges that position; other types: nothing |
| runtime package publish-drafts | `TYPE/NAME` per published item, `app/APPNAME` per unhidden app | `position/NAME` entries only; an app name is no package id, so nothing |
| artifact reload (`MetadataPlugin._reloadAndAnnounce`) | the artifact's file path, or the HMR body's own list | a path names nothing: carries nothing, waits for the boot run |

Carried at the next restart, as before: a hot upgrade over a version the running kernel still serves (its old position keeps serving, so it reads as still declared), and the runtime `POST /packages` install and enable routes, which do not announce.

## Tests

35 tests in `position-renamed-holder-carry.test.ts`, the carry's existing harness, all green.

- **Condition 2 on the reload path, both ways, through the announcing doors (real `ObjectKernel`).** The doors' payloads are spelled as each door spells them.
  - A reload naming a package whose position claims a name another package holds: refused `held-by-other`, said once, nothing moves.
  - An uninstall's announcement (a withdrawn package): nothing is judged.
  - A hot install of another package, followed by a per-item publish naming its positions: the announced package's own rename is carried, and the standing claim it did not name is not judged.
- **Hot install pin.** v1 uninstalled, then v2 hot-installed: the holder moves with no restart, the CONTROL holder is untouched, and a repeat install is a no-op. A hot upgrade over v1 leaves no holder on an unserved position.
- **`positionRenameReloadScope`, per announcer.** `app/ID` counts while the package is held and not once it is withdrawn. `position/NAME` counts. Another type, an app name that is not a package, a file path, no payload and malformed entries all name nothing. A reload that names nothing reads nothing.
- **Left-behind read (finding 2).** The boot run reads pending `sys_approval_request` rows. A reload that moves no row reads none. A reload that moves a row reads them and names the request.
- **Runner.** Reloads before the boot run are ignored, a standing refusal is not repeated, runs never overlap, and a failed run does not block the next one.

## Acceptance notes

- Ruling A1 (record 6841971722): "when the renamed definition loads, the platform moves that position's HOLDERS (`sys_user_position.position` old → new) in every organization, as the system, idempotently". Conditions 1 to 3 are judged by the same code on both paths. Condition 2 is now pinned on the reload path as well.
- Owed outside this PR (seat-filed): the ADR-0150 D7 addendum sentence "It runs at boot only", the `PositionSchema.renamedFrom` describe text and the `packages/spec/liveness/position.json` line; the runtime announce card for `POST /packages` and enable; and the finding that a re-register of an installed id leaves the previous version's items served.
- This card stays open for the hot-upgrade path and the non-announcing doors.
